page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory. For high-speed local data handling, the configuration includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates advanced instruction extensions, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES and VAES.

Benchmark results place the D96ads_v7 in the top tier for compute and memory performance. The system registered 176145.96 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 117050.24. Memory throughput reached 311.62 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 174.65 GB/sec in write operations. High-throughput data processing is demonstrated by single-threaded gzip compression achieving 41.25 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 610.83 GB/sec. Application testing showed static web serving throughput of 91.12 GB/sec and 140.26 million Redis SET operations per second.

In qualitative resource density, the server balances 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside an expansive 5.67 TB local NVMe disk tier. While it lacks specialized discrete GPU accelerators, its AVX-512 vector support enables CPU-bound machine learning tasks, delivering 5540.41 tokens per second during small model prompt processing. The primary hardware tradeoff is the reliance on a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, which is balanced rather than heavily memory-skewed, combined with ephemeral local storage.

The D96ads_v7 is suited for enterprise relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching tiers, large-scale web serving infrastructures, batch analytics, and continuous integration pipelines requiring high local I/O performance.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It provides 384.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, and integrates 5670 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. In benchmarking, the server demonstrated top-tier multi-threaded performance, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 117050.24, multi-core stress-ng score of 176145.96, and over 140 million Redis operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 311.62 GB/sec on large read blocks, augmented by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. Combining balanced compute, extensive memory bandwidth, and substantial local NVMe capacity, this instance is well suited for high-throughput database workloads, large-scale caching engines, data engineering pipelines, and dense containerized application clusters.
